newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Apr 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Apr 30.

text.p: Coalition's credibility concerns Bolger: Prime Minister admitted to concern on Tuesday about his one-seat majority government's credibility after further revelations of NZ First MP Tukoroirangi Morgan's taxpayer-funded spending. Page 1.

Kindergarten associations shocked by urgency move: The government's surprise use of Parliament's urgency rles to try to remove kindergarten teachers from the State Sector Act had been a shock, the Free Kindergarten Associations said on Tuesday. Page 2.

PM against locking in super: Prime Minister Jim Bolger on Tuesday poured cold water on the bid by Treasurer Winston Peters to have the compulsory superannuation scheme entrenched by legislation if it is passed by referendum. Page 2.
Dope party saw MP as recruit: Associate Treasurer Tuariki Delamere said on Tuesday that Aotearoa Legalise Cannabis Party had invited him to join it after he admitted he had smoked cannabis. Page 2.

Proposal rejected: Cabinet ministers rejected a proposal put forward by Social Welfare Minister Roger Sowry to take away special benefits of $10 or less from recipients after six months rather than a year, a government spokesman said on Tuesday. Page 2.
Agencies compete for referendum campaign: Seven companies have put in tenders to run the public education campaign leading up to September's referendum on compulsory superannuation. Page 2.

Glenbrook may close within two years: BHP NZ Steel chief executive Malcolm Burns on Tuesday vowed to keep the billion-dollar Glenbrook steel plant open in the face of owner BHP's decision to close it. Page 13.

Fund managers less bullish -- survey: Fund managers are slightly less bullish on their outlook for New Zealand property and equities than in January, according to a survey by the Alexander Consulting Group. Page 13.

NZ, Australia 'lagging behind' with reforms: New Zealand was showing signs of "losing the plot" and Australia was not much better, Business Roundtable vice-chairman Bob Matthew said in Sydney on Tuesday night. Page 13.
Telecom reduces data costs: Telecom announced price cuts of up to 30 percent on its digital data transmission products on Tuesday and signalled further cuts. Page 13.

Otter Gold's output slips 17 percent: Otter Gold's share of gold output from its two producing mines slipped more than 17 percent to 22,020 ounces in the three months till March, compared with the previous three months. Page 14.

Kupe field shows more promise: Seismic work off the Taranaki coast has identified a new prospect in the south of the Kupe field, with gas reserves in the central area possibly larger than expected as well, New Zealand Oil and Gas said on Tuesday. Page 14.

Macraes puts case for mine expansion: The proposed $120 million expansion of the Macraes mine would generate an estimate $1.4 billion in revenue for the Macraes Mining Company, operations manager Wayne Seabrook said on Tuesday. Page 14.
